related_questions.question: How long do COVID germs stay in the air?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 virus particles can remain airborne for hours, potentially lingering in the air after an infected person has left the space. Studies suggest the virus can stay airborne for up to 3 hours. Factors like ventilation and room size can influence how long the virus remains airborne according to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (.gov).

list.title: Airborne Transmission:
list.snippet: COVID-19 can be spread through the air via small droplets and particles, which can linger in the air for extended periods.

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: Research indicates that the virus can remain viable in the air for up to 3 hours, according to WebMD.

list.title: Factors Affecting Duration:
list.snippet: Ventilation systems, room size, and the presence of air filtration systems can impact how long the virus stays airborne.

list.title: Persistence:
list.snippet: The virus can be present in the air even after an infected person has left the space.

related_questions.title: Advice for the public: Coronavirus disease (COVID-19)

text_blocks.snippet: To protect yourself from COVID-19, the most effective strategies include vaccination, physical distancing, wearing a mask, and practicing good hygiene. Vaccination, when available, is a crucial step in building immunity. Maintaining physical distance of at least one meter from others, even if they appear healthy, can significantly reduce transmission. Wearing a mask, especially in crowded or poorly ventilated areas, adds an extra layer of protection. Additionally, frequent handwashing with soap and water or using an alcohol-based hand rub, along with covering coughs and sneezes, helps prevent the spread of the virus. If you experience symptoms or test positive, self-isolate to prevent further transmission.

list.title: Masks:
list.snippet: Wear a mask in public settings, particularly when physical distancing is difficult or in poorly ventilated areas.

list.title: Hygiene:
list.snippet: Wash your hands frequently with soap and water or use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer. Cover coughs and sneezes with your elbow or a tissue, and dispose of used tissues properly.

list.title: Self-Isolation:
list.snippet: If you develop symptoms or test positive, isolate yourself to prevent further spread of the virus.
